text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock has fallen 1.2% today and nearly 18% over two weeks, tracking a sharp decline that accelerated after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 3rd. While oil prices have held relatively steady (US crude at $99.64/barrel), refineries are running near capacity at 94.5%, which normally supports margins—but the market has clearly reacted negatively to the company's reported financial results, suggesting profits or guidance disappointed despite decent operational conditions.

The broader headwind is political: Democrats swept the midterm elections, which shifts energy policy toward renewable energy support and away from fossil fuels. That's a structural concern for a refiner, though it doesn't directly move oil prices day-to-day. The two-week decline suggests investors are repricing how they view the refining business in a changing energy landscape, independent of current crude costs or refinery utilization rates.
